scenes.say: Are concurrency and parallelism just two words for the same thing? Let's clear that up.

scenes.label: Concurrency
scenes.sub: Tasks make progress together, but not always at the exact same time.
scenes.say: Concurrency means multiple tasks are making progress together, but not always at the exact same time.

scenes.label: Parallelism
scenes.sub: Tasks run truly simultaneously, usually on multiple CPU cores.
scenes.say: Parallelism is when tasks are actually running at the same time, usually on multiple CPU cores.
Concurrency is about interleaving tasks, while parallelism is about running tasks at the exact same time.

scenes.question: Are threads always parallel?
scenes.wrong: Yes, threads always run in parallel.
scenes.right: No, threads can be concurrent without being parallel.
scenes.say: Here's a common interview trap: are threads always parallel? No—they can be concurrent without actually running at the same time.
